rationale: The printed entry's core is carried by the exact reference cluster: Name is repeatedly located on/at the ark-house (2 Sam 6:2; 7:13; 1 Kgs 8:20-21), the ark is inventoried as containing precisely three items (Heb 9:4), and each item is independently defined by Scripture as the Head's Word (Deut 8:3), covenant law (Deut 4:13), and fruitful priesthood (Num 17:5, 8). Isa 4:1 and Ex 20:7 then supply the counterfeit/vain clauses without remainder. This cross-text mechanics is tighter than the generic character/authority reading for the same verses; the latter flattens the ark inventory and house-Name equation into mere presence language and leaves the three-item substance and the Isa 4:1 refusal of provision unexplained. No supplied detail contradicts the entry or is better handled by the counter.
book_core_identification: Name = the covenant identity of a house, consisting of its Head's Word, covenant law, and fruitful priesthood.
book_secondary_elaborations: Substituting any one of the three creates a counterfeit Name
Rejecting, replacing, or removing any one takes the Name in vain
chapter_only_objections: Extension of the definition to the petitions of the Lord's Prayer
Marriage/bride typology and headship applications beyond Isa 4:1
Beast/Lamb forehead-name contrast and disciple-sealing segue
strongest_counter_interpretation: In the cited texts 'Name' still means God's own revealed identity, presence, and authority that dwells above the ark and in the temple; the ark's contents are the separate covenant tokens that accompany that presence, not the definitional substance of the Name itself.
counter_core_identification: Name = God's (or the person's) revealed identity, presence, reputation, and authority.
material_core_denial: The Name does not consist of the Head's Word + covenant law + fruitful priesthood as the covenant identity of a house; those are only associated tokens while Name remains the divine person's own character/presence.
counter_case: Standard 'Name theology' already accounts for 2 Sam 6–7 and 1 Kgs 8 as the Name dwelling at the sanctuary without equating Name to the three contents
Heb 9:4 simply lists cultic relics; it never calls them 'the Name'
Broader biblical usage (Ex 34:5-7, Prov 18:10, Acts 4:12, etc.) treats Name as personal character/authority, which the tripartite house formula does not naturally cover
book_explanatory_advantages: Unifies the precise reference list printed with the entry into one coherent symbol via explicit content definitions
Explains why the ark is said to have its 'name called by the name of the LORD' and why the house is built 'for my name' only after the ark is placed inside
Gives concrete mechanical content to 'take the Name in vain' and to Isa 4:1's demand for the name while refusing the man's bread and apparel
Accounts for the three-item inventory as necessary rather than incidental
counter_explanatory_advantages: Aligns with the dominant lexical and theological consensus on shem/onoma
Requires fewer constructive steps outside any single verse
decisive_sources: Deut 8:3; 4:13; Num 17:5, 8 (independent definitions of the three items)
